newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's TA Bank accorded D-2 rating by DCR.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's TA Bank accorded D-2 rating by DCR.

text.p: Rating agency Duff & Phelps (DCR) said on Wednesday it had accorded Malaysian-owned TA Bank of South Africa an investment grade rating of D-2.
The rating defined it as an organisation with a good capacity to timeously honour its depositor obligations.
TA Bank of South Africa was officially launched in the country on July 16.
DCR senior bank analyst Charles Nel said the rating was accorded on the basis that TA Bank demonstrated all the characteristics necessary to succeeds as a niche bank in the South African market.

"The capital base has been well established from the outset (total capital will exceed 300 million rand shortly), the bank will maintain a high liquid position, senior management are all conservative bankers with many years experience in the local banking industry and emphasis is being placed on a high quality lending book, with no involvement in higher risk trading activities," Nel said.
Additional comfort was obtained from the fact that the bank's parent company -- Malaysia's TA Enterprises Berhad -- had confirmed it would provide capital and liquidity support as and when necessary.
